Who Proximus Global is

Proximus Global is the international digital communications operation of Proximus Group, combining BICS, Telesign and Route Mobile into a complementary portfolio spanning connectivity, customer engagement and digital trust. BICS supplies the carrier-grade network layer, including global voice and messaging, roaming, mobile data, IoT, fraud-prevention and cloud-communications capabilities. Telesign provides programmable communications, verification and digital-identity services, while Route Mobile contributes a scaled CPaaS platform, omnichannel engagement capabilities, extensive emerging-market reach and application-to-person messaging solutions. Together, these businesses cover the digital customer lifecycle: connecting enterprises and operators, enabling brands to engage customers through messaging and digital channels, and protecting interactions through identity and fraud controls. Investor materials position the combined international portfolio as an end-to-end proposition that competitors generally cannot match across mobility, CPaaS, identity and carrier connectivity. The Group completed its majority acquisition of Route Mobile in May 2024, extending its international footprint and product breadth. Proximus Global reports reach exceeding five billion subscribers, more than 180 billion secured transactions annually and connectivity to over 1,000 destinations. Its strategic rationale is to exploit product, geographic and go-to-market complementarities, create cross-selling and operating synergies, and increase Proximus Group's exposure to global digital communications markets beyond infrastructure-dependent domestic telecom revenue.

The three brands

Independent go-to-market brands · shared strategic parent · complementary layers of the digital-communications stack.

Carrier-grade network layer

Global voice, messaging, roaming, mobile data, IoT, fraud-prevention and cloud-communications for operators & enterprises.

Digital identity & trust

Programmable communications, verification, phone-number intelligence and fraud prevention — securing 180 billion+ transactions annually.

Global CPaaS & engagement

Cloud communications, omnichannel messaging (SMS, RCS, voice, WhatsApp, email), CX and marketing platforms across 1,000+ destinations.

BICS, Telesign and Route Mobile form a deliberately complementary three-brand portfolio. BICS is the connectivity foundation: a global carrier and communications-platform business operating voice, messaging, roaming, mobile data, IoT and fraud-prevention services through an extensive network of operator relationships. Telesign supplies the protect layer, combining programmable communications with digital identity, verification and intelligence capabilities used by major digital enterprises across more than 230 countries and territories. Route Mobile strengthens the engage layer through scaled CPaaS, application-to-person messaging and omnichannel customer-engagement capabilities, with especially strong reach in India, Asia-Pacific, Africa and Latin America. Proximus Group's acquisition thesis was that no single brand covered the complete value chain, but together they could connect users and enterprises, orchestrate multichannel communications and secure digital interactions. Proximus Global therefore preserves established customer-facing brands while coordinating product development, routes to market, network assets and cross-selling. The portfolio is intended to generate revenue growth, more efficient delivery and synergies from shared scale, while reducing Proximus Group's dependence on domestic network-linked revenue.

The strategic north star

Bold2025 is the current active plan across Proximus Group. Every commercial, technology and CRM decision (this RFP included) is measured against these ambitions.

Proximus investor materials reviewed for FY2023 and FY2024 describe the active strategic cycle as bold2025, not Bold2028. Bold2025 was launched in January 2023 around the purpose of boldly building a connected world that people trust so society blooms. It combines three enabling strengths with three stakeholder outcomes. The strengths are deploying Belgium's number-one gigabit network, engineering technology assets that enable digital ecosystems, and fostering an engaged culture with empowered ways of working. The outcomes are delivering an unrivalled customer experience, growing profitably through strong domestic and international brands, and acting sustainably and inclusively. Operational targets included more than three million fiber-connectable premises and approximately 50% fiber coverage by end-2025, near-complete 5G indoor coverage in the 2025-2026 timeframe, roughly EUR 70 million of IT total-cost-of-ownership reduction by 2025, sustained cybersecurity resilience and profitable international growth. Route Mobile was intended to accelerate the global pillar by adding CPaaS scale, emerging-market coverage and substantial synergy potential. No Bold2028 plan was identified in the specified reporting-period materials.

AI & digital transformation posture

The AI and platform posture matters directly to the CRM debate — Copilot, Foundry, Fabric and the wider Microsoft AI stack land natively into a Bold2025-aligned direction.

Proximus presents AI and digitalization as operating-model capabilities rather than isolated products. Its priorities include modernizing IT and network platforms, using data and AI to improve customer journeys, automate network operations and accelerate employee productivity, while maintaining cybersecurity, privacy and European sovereignty. Proximus Ada serves as the Group's Belgian center of excellence for AI and cybersecurity. FY2023 initiatives included an internal secure generative-AI chat service, trials of Microsoft 365 Copilot, developer-focused GitHub Copilot adoption and AI-enabled digital platforms. The strategy couples experimentation with governance, reskilling and measurable efficiency, while Proximus Global extends AI into fraud prevention, identity intelligence, CPaaS personalization and trusted digital engagement.

Risks to plan against

Risk register extracted from Proximus Group disclosures. Every CRM answer should be defendable against these.

R01

Structural decline in legacy international voice traffic and associated revenue.

R02

Pricing pressure and commoditization in application-to-person messaging and authentication SMS.

R03

Execution risk in integrating Route Mobile with BICS and Telesign and realizing planned synergies.

R04

Intense Belgian competition from converged operators, fiber builds and the new mobile entrant DIGI.

R05

High fiber and 5G capital requirements can constrain free cash flow and increase leverage.

R06

Cybersecurity, privacy, data-sovereignty and regulatory obligations are material operational risks.

R07

Rapid technology shifts in CPaaS, digital identity, network APIs and generative AI may require continued investment.

R08

Foreign-exchange, geopolitical and emerging-market exposure affects the international portfolio.

The 3 pricing scenarios (all mandatory)

Option 1

BICS CRM migration only

Standalone migration of BICS Salesforce Sales Cloud + Service Cloud into the target CRM. Includes functional config, data migration, integrations with retained systems, user enablement, cutover, hypercare. TeleSign and Route Mobile CRM remain out of scope. Coexistence assumptions required.

Option 2

BU2 consolidation only

TeleSign + Route Mobile + affiliates consolidated into the target CRM. Harmonisation of BU2 CRM capabilities, processes, data models, integrations. Explicit assumptions, dependencies and transition constraints for the BU2 perimeter.

Option 3

TeleSign CRM migration only

Standalone migration of TeleSign Salesforce environment into the target CRM. Full-scope migration activities. Coexistence with BICS and Route Mobile CRMs required. Costs of retained SaaS ecosystem tools must be explicitly identified.

Key principles from Proximus

Configuration before customization

OOTB capabilities prioritised. Custom development must be justified by business value, technical necessity, or compliance.

AI-first, governed by design

AI-first approach — provided usage is governed, auditable, secure and compliant.

API-first integration model

API-first architecture for robust integration, simple connectivity, future extensibility.

Cloud-first strategy

Cloud-first, aligned with Proximus security, data residency, operational and compliance requirements.

Commercial terms — hard rules

  • Initial commitment: 3 to 5 years, renewable by mutual agreement.
  • Bid remains binding for 12 months from submission.
  • Prices remain the maximum for 7 years after first order acceptance.
  • Software, subscriptions, support & maintenance must remain available for minimum 7 years.
  • Currencies accepted: EUR, USD, or INR (Incoterms DDP Belgium, incl. taxes except VAT).
  • Modular pricing required — no all-in package pricing only.
  • SaaS conditions must all be met: min 18-month subscription · Proximus keeps portability options · Proximus may refuse upgrades · full cost breakdown transparency.
  • Legal entity invoicing: BICS, TeleSign, Route Mobile must be invoiceable separately under a common framework.
  • 5-year TCO table mandatory per pricing scenario, broken down by cost component and year.

The RFP process, step by step

1. Receipt & intention to bid

Acknowledge receipt by email; confirm whether you will bid and want to be in the selection process. Provide names of technical, commercial and signing contacts.

2. Q&A

Bidder is encouraged to ask questions. Proximus Global will be available to answer questions sent 1 working day in advance during a call of maximum 1 hour. Proximus Global reserves the right not to answer questions beyond mere clarification.

3. Bid submission

Submit by email to the three named contacts, with a signed cover letter stating company name, VAT number, RFP reference, and a list of all documents.

4. Evaluation

Proximus Global may request clarifications, additional information, or issue additional requirements as they surface. The bids with the highest evaluation scores are shortlisted.

5. Workshop (shortlisted only)

Agenda and workshop questions sent upfront. Bidder presentations provided at workshop start. An updated bid is submitted after the workshop.

6. Supplier selection

Proximus Global informs the selected supplier. Non-shortlisted bidders may request a debriefing (points-of-improvement only, no comparison with the selected bid).

Non-binding, one-sided: Proximus Global may cancel or change the RFP at any time with no liability. No minimum order commitment. All bidder costs borne by the bidder. Bids are binding on the bidder for 12 months.

The RFP Body — narrative sections

The prose sections of the main RFP: transformation vision, business scope, technical & security expectations, commercials, service levels, and RFP process rules.

Section 2 — Transformation vision & scope

2.1 CRM transformation vision

Integrated, scalable and future-ready CRM platform across business units and legal entities, while ensuring autonomy and data segregation. AI-driven to harmonise customer-facing processes, strengthen data quality and governance, improve visibility, and enable data-driven decisions by Senior Management.

2.2 RFP object

Select a bidder to support the selection and implementation of a strategic CRM platform. Solution must cover Core and Extended CRM features across Marketing, Sales, Commercial Contract Management, Business Operations and Customer Operations Support. Consolidation may be delivered through waves and multiple scenarios.

CRM Core Features

  • Lead management and conversion
  • Marketing Campaign
  • Customer and Account Management
  • Opportunity Management
  • Revenue intelligence and Forecasting
  • Sales Automation
  • Product Catalogue
  • Customer Operations (ticketing system)
  • Reporting and Analytics

CRM Extended Features

  • Lead Routing flows
  • Marketing Automation
  • CPQ
  • Database Enrichment
  • Account Plan
  • BID flow Management
  • Contract Lifecycle Management
  • Contract Signature
  • Sales Operation enablement
  • Sales Incentive Management
  • Support Centre

Core / Extended split defines scope categories. Binding MoSCoW prioritisation is at requirement level in Appendix A.

2.4 Future vision — 5 key principles

  • Target operating model — common CRM capabilities, harmonised data, scalable architecture that evolves with the business.
  • Unified platform, phased rollout — one strategic platform, wave-based rollout, entity-level data segregation, ability to separate a BU's data and configuration without full re-implementation.
  • Configuration before customization — OOTB prioritised, custom development justified only by business value, technical necessity, or compliance.
  • AI-first, governed by design — governed, auditable, secure, compliant AI.
  • API-first, cloud-first — extensible integration and cloud strategy aligned to Proximus security, residency, ops and compliance requirements.

Section 5 — Other requirements

5.1 Infrastructure & Deployment

DCV requirements (Appendix B) part of evaluation. On-prem architecture compatibility, virtualization environments, related constraints.

5.2 Data migration workstream (integral to the project)

  • Migration tooling & execution — scripts, ETL, AI tools; automation, monitoring, error handling, repeatability, auditability.
  • Source data assessment — objects, fields, relationships, attachments, historical records, ownership, volumes, dependencies.
  • Data quality, cleansing, enrichment — duplicates, obsolete, incomplete, inconsistent data resolved before migration.
  • Data mapping and transformation — source-to-target mappings, transformation rules, picklist harmonisation, legacy IDs, traceability.
  • Testing and validation — trial migrations, reconciliation, completeness, UAT, formal sign-off.
  • Cutover, rollback, business continuity — cutover plan, data freeze, delta migration, go-live readiness, rollback, communications.
  • Post-migration stabilisation — monitoring, defect resolution, reports/integrations validated, transition to steady state.
  • Migration methodology & governance — phases, deliverables, decision gates, roles, tracking.
  • Security, privacy, compliance — access controls, encryption, masking/anonymisation, retention, privacy compliance.
  • Assumptions, dependencies, limitations — explicit prerequisites, customer responsibilities, excluded data sets.

5.3 Change Management, Training & Knowledge Transfer

  • Training strategy & scope — for admins, developers, ops, business key users, managers, end users.
  • Role-based training paths.
  • Instructor-led, virtual, self-paced, hands-on, train-the-trainer, certification paths.
  • Training materials, user & admin guides, developer docs, quick reference cards, KB articles.
  • Knowledge transfer to operational teams — architecture, config, integrations, data model, security, release, monitoring, troubleshooting.
  • Change impact assessment on roles, processes, data ownership, reporting, governance.
  • Stakeholder engagement & communication plan.
  • Super-user & champion network.
  • User readiness & adoption measurement.
  • Go-live support and reinforcement.
  • Costs explicitly identified (licences, certifications, travel, 3rd-party content).

Executive view

Executive summary

AI-generated response draft · human validation required before submission.Content is grounded in reviewed Microsoft Learn pages and every requirement answer is backed by real Microsoft product evidence with verified references. No compliance option, commercial commitment, implementation estimate, contractual position, certification, privacy attestation, or customer-specific design is approved by this draft. Items flagged for human validation must be completed by the accountable Microsoft, legal, privacy, security, licensing, engineering, or delivery owner.

Recommended position

One governed customer platform, without forcing one operating model on every entity.

Position Microsoft AI Business Solutions as the configurable foundation for phased harmonization across BICS, TeleSign, Route Mobile, and future entities. Dynamics 365, Dataverse, Power Platform, and Copilot Studio provide the CRM, workflow, data, and agent core. Microsoft 365 and Azure strengthen that core where collaboration, productivity, event-driven integration, or specialist cloud services are required. This is a solution hypothesis pending detailed architecture, product-fit, licensing, security, and delivery validation.

01

Strategic alignment

Proximus Global asks for a unified, scalable, cloud-first and API-first platform delivered in waves. Lead with the AI Business Solutions core: establish common Dataverse foundations, add Dynamics 365 workloads by business priority, extend approved processes with Copilot Studio, and govern change through solutions and pipelines.

02

Requirement posture

The response preserves all 191 Appendix A requirements. Every answer is grounded in real Microsoft product evidence with 4 verified Microsoft Learn references. Verdicts follow the RFP-defined scale, and each answer notes the per-brand delta from BICS, TeleSign and Route Mobile Appendix C volumes.

03

Transformation logic

The current estate is not one migration: BICS and TeleSign run separate Salesforce ecosystems, while Route Mobile combines CRM with Odoo sales, product, billing, accounting, and helpdesk processes. The Microsoft proposition therefore leads with phased coexistence and controlled convergence.

Why Microsoft

A platform case, not a feature checklist

01

Common foundation, modular adoption

Dataverse provides the shared data and security foundation; Dynamics 365 and Power Platform capabilities can be introduced by scope and wave.

02

Governance from design through release

Role-based access, auditing, solutions, pipelines, and Azure DevOps tooling align platform control with the requested operating and release model.

03

AI within operational workflows

Dynamics 365 Copilot capabilities and Copilot Studio agents and workflows create a path to governed assistance and action in the flow of work, subject to use-case, evaluation, tool, data, and human-review controls.

04

Integration and analytics adjacency

Dataverse APIs, connectors, virtual tables, Power Automate, Power BI, and selective Azure services support an API-first and event-driven architecture without claiming that every named integration is standard.

Better together

AI Business Solutions at the core, Microsoft Cloud where it adds evidence-based value

Core

Dynamics 365

Sales, Customer Service, and Customer Insights provide the principal customer-facing application workloads assessed against the RFP.

Core

Power Platform and Copilot Studio

Dataverse, Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, Power Pages, and Copilot Studio provide the data, extension, automation, analytics, portal, agent, and workflow foundation.

Work layer

Microsoft 365

Teams and Microsoft 365 experiences can bring collaboration and approved agents closer to users. Appendix C confirms existing Teams, Exchange, and Copilot for Sales touchpoints; entitlements remain unverified.

Cloud extension

Azure

Use Azure selectively for event-driven integration and specialist services where validated requirements exceed the core platform. The reviewed Event Grid connector supports Power Automate and Copilot Studio; each service requires separate design and commercial validation.

Business value

Benefits measured from a customer baseline

Value hypothesisMeasureEvidence method
Seller productivityTime in manual account, opportunity, quote, approval, forecast, and activity tasksBaseline task study; measure minutes per transaction and adoption by role.

01

Base case

Use contracted prices, approved scope, phased active users, quoted implementation, and current operating-cost baselines.

02

Sensitivity

Recalculate for user counts, rollout delay, data volume, ISV price, implementation effort, dual-run duration, and benefit realization at low / base / high values.

03

Self-critique

License overlap, attach rights, capacity growth, migration quality, telecom product complexity, and delayed decommissioning can materially change the result.

04

Decision gate

Publish ROI and payback only after Finance approves the baseline, benefit ownership, attribution method, discount rate, and scenario assumptions.

Demonstration strategy

Suggested demo personas and stories

AI-generated response draft · human validation required before submission.Content is grounded in reviewed Microsoft Learn pages and every requirement answer is backed by real Microsoft product evidence with verified references. No compliance option, commercial commitment, implementation estimate, contractual position, certification, privacy attestation, or customer-specific design is approved by this draft. Items flagged for human validation must be completed by the accountable Microsoft, legal, privacy, security, licensing, engineering, or delivery owner.

One connected narrative, five roles

Demonstrate the path from account insight through complex offer, approval, service, fulfillment, and governed change. The personas are fictional and tailored to the RFP; customer stories supply inspiration only.

01

Fictional Proximus demo persona

Elena — Global enterprise account director

Moment that matters: Prepare for a strategic multinational customer meeting without assembling context from three CRM estates.

Story arc: Open a governed global account hierarchy; summarize recent interactions and open service issues; identify related opportunities across BICS, TeleSign, and Route Mobile; draft a meeting brief; collaborate in Teams; record agreed actions.

Demonstration stack: Dynamics 365 Sales, Dataverse, Microsoft 365 integration, Copilot subject to approval

Proposed validation measures: Time to prepare; missing-data rate; follow-up completion; seller acceptance.

Microsoft customer-story inspiration: Verizon chose Dynamics 365 Sales to improve seller efficiency; Lenovo used Dynamics 365 for a standardized global view and digital sales transformation.

Proof boundary: This is a proposed fictional scenario. Use representative Proximus data and acceptance criteria; do not reuse another customer's outcome as a Proximus forecast.

02

Fictional Proximus demo persona

Marc — Global deal-desk manager

Moment that matters: Turn a complex multi-entity telecom offer into a compliant, approved, signed contract without spreadsheet acrobatics.

Story arc: Select a representative bundle; apply commercial terms and compatibility rules; route discount and legal approvals; compare native quote coverage with a shortlisted CPQ/CLM extension; generate a customer-facing document; preserve the audit trail.

Demonstration stack: Dynamics 365 Sales, Power Automate, Dataverse, shortlisted CPQ and CLM candidates

Proposed validation measures: Quote cycle time; manual handoffs; approval exceptions; pricing accuracy.

Microsoft customer-story inspiration: G&J Pepsi demonstrates cross-functional process automation with Dynamics 365, Dataverse, and Power Automate; it is process inspiration, not telecom CPQ proof.

Proof boundary: This is a proposed fictional scenario. Use representative Proximus data and acceptance criteria; do not reuse another customer's outcome as a Proximus forecast.

03

Fictional Proximus demo persona

Sofia — Enterprise customer service agent

Moment that matters: Resolve a customer issue with complete relationship, service, and commercial context while respecting entity visibility rules.

Story arc: Accept an email or chat case; identify account and entitlement; review interaction and opportunity context; surface knowledge; route to the right specialist; collaborate in Teams; summarize resolution and create a governed follow-up.

Demonstration stack: Dynamics 365 Customer Service, unified routing, knowledge, Dataverse, Teams, Copilot subject to approval

Proposed validation measures: Handle time; transfer rate; first-contact resolution; SLA attainment; knowledge reuse.

Microsoft customer-story inspiration: Gardens Alive integrated voice, chat, and email with third-party connectors and unified routing, reporting more than 7% improvement in customer-service delivery.

Proof boundary: This is a proposed fictional scenario. Use representative Proximus data and acceptance criteria; do not reuse another customer's outcome as a Proximus forecast.

04

Fictional Proximus demo persona

Ravi — Service fulfillment coordinator

Moment that matters: Carry a sold enterprise service into fulfillment without losing product, site, contact, or commitment data.

Story arc: Convert an approved commercial request into a work item; validate prerequisites; assign the responsible team; expose status to sales and service; capture completion evidence; trigger billing-readiness review; notify the account team.

Demonstration stack: Dataverse, Power Automate, Dynamics 365 workflow; Field Service only if validated as in scope

Proposed validation measures: Handoff defects; status inquiries; elapsed time; rework; completion-data quality.

Microsoft customer-story inspiration: G&J Pepsi connected sales requests to work orders, scheduling, mobile execution, and service reporting using Dynamics 365, Dataverse, Power Automate, and Power Apps.

Proof boundary: This is a proposed fictional scenario. Use representative Proximus data and acceptance criteria; do not reuse another customer's outcome as a Proximus forecast.

05

Fictional Proximus demo persona

Amina — Global CRM platform owner

Moment that matters: Introduce a shared process safely across entities while retaining justified local controls.

Story arc: Review a requested change; assess data and security impact; configure in a solution; run automated checks; promote through governed environments; inspect auditing and adoption dashboards; roll back or remediate based on acceptance results.

Demonstration stack: Power Platform environments, security, auditing, solutions, pipelines, Azure DevOps, Power BI

Proposed validation measures: Deployment lead time; failed changes; policy exceptions; adoption; support volume.

Microsoft customer-story inspiration: ABN AMRO is cited by Microsoft as using Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service and lowering customer-engagement-platform TCO by up to 40%; Lenovo provides the standardized global-system pattern.

Proof boundary: This is a proposed fictional scenario. Use representative Proximus data and acceptance criteria; do not reuse another customer's outcome as a Proximus forecast.

Recommended demo sequence

Lead with Elena's global-account moment, pass the opportunity to Marc for commercial control, show Sofia handling a connected service issue, continue through Ravi's fulfillment handoff, and close with Amina proving governance. Use one synthetic customer and one traceable data thread throughout.

GBB · 22 additions

Clarification register · GBB additions

Resolve before claims become commitments

These 22 clarifications from the GBB draft complement Sam's cover-to-cover re-audit. They target open inputs that materially affect solution fit, licensing, security, migration, delivery, and TCO.

Decision Critical Which three measurable business outcomes will determine platform selection, and what are their current baselines? Executive sponsor / Finance Prevents requirement coverage from substituting for an approved value case.
Decision Critical How will functional fit, architecture, security, migration risk, user adoption, commercial value, and vendor viability be weighted in the final score? Procurement Makes the award logic testable and aligns response emphasis.
Scoring Critical How are Must, Should, and Could requirements weighted, and does failure to meet any Must requirement create a pass/fail or exclusion gate? Procurement / Evaluation committee Clarifies whether priority changes points or determines eligibility.
Scoring Critical What score is assigned to each compliance response: Fully Compliant with OOTB Features, Fully Compliant with Customization, Future Compliant, Partially Compliant, and Not Compliant? Procurement / Evaluation committee Makes the Appendix A compliance scale quantitatively testable.
Scoring Critical Are there minimum technical, security, privacy, functional, commercial, or overall score thresholds that a bid must meet to be shortlisted? Procurement / Evaluation committee Identifies award gates that are not disclosed in the RFP.
Scoring Critical How are the workshop, configured demonstrations, clarification responses, and updated bid scored, and do they replace or adjust the initial written-bid score? Procurement / Evaluation committee Clarifies how shortlist-stage evidence affects final ranking.
Scope Critical Which processes and user groups are in each rollout wave for BICS, TeleSign, and Route Mobile? Program sponsor Controls licensing quantities, coexistence, migration, and delivery scope.
Scope High Which local processes and data boundaries must remain entity-specific, and which must become global standards? Business process owners Defines the common core without flattening justified autonomy.
Users Critical For each role, how many users require full create/update rights, light participation, approval-only access, analytics, portal access, or AI assistance? Business owners / Licensing Replaces entity-level indicators with a defensible license persona model.
Sales High What sales methodology, opportunity types, territory rules, split-credit rules, forecast hierarchy, and currency behavior must be standardized? Sales leadership Determines Sales configuration and acceptance scenarios.
CPQ Critical Provide representative complex offers, compatibility rules, pricing formulas, discount authorities, currencies, taxes, and quote documents for scripted CPQ testing. Product / Deal desk Native versus ISV fit cannot be decided without real telecom configurations.
Catalog and billing Critical Where are commercial, technical, resource, rating, billing, and entitlement masters today, and which system owns each in the target architecture? Product / Billing architecture Prevents CRM from being positioned as an unproven telecom BSS replacement.
Contracts High Which clause, redlining, approval, signature, obligation, renewal, repository, and retention capabilities are mandatory for CLM? Legal / Commercial operations Creates an evidence-led CLM shortlist and demonstration script.
Service High Which case types, channels, SLAs, entitlements, routing rules, knowledge sources, escalations, and customer self-service journeys are in scope? Service operations Defines Customer Service, channel, and portal requirements.
Data Critical What are source record counts, duplicate rates, data-quality thresholds, retention periods, legal holds, archival needs, and mastered-data ownership? Data owner / Privacy Sizes migration, storage, cleansing, reconciliation, and governance.
Integration Critical Provide the authoritative interface inventory with owners, direction, frequency, volume, latency, identity, error handling, and continuity requirements. Enterprise architecture Converts named applications into testable interface contracts.
Security Critical Which data residency, segregation, privileged access, encryption, audit, retention, incident, recovery, and regulatory controls are award gates? CISO / Privacy / Legal Separates product capability from required control evidence and attestations.
AI High Which AI use cases are approved for phase one, what data may they use, and what human review, evaluation, logging, geography, and language controls apply? AI governance / Legal Constrains the Copilot proposition to governed and measurable use cases.
Operations High Who will own environments, releases, support, monitoring, data quality, automation, integrations, ISVs, and continuous improvement after go-live? Platform owner Defines the sustainable operating model and run cost.
Commercial Critical Will bidders receive a common five-year pricing workbook covering phased users, capacities, support, implementation, ISVs, dual run, inflation, and exit costs? Procurement / Finance Enables a like-for-like TCO comparison.
Delivery High What migration windows, blackout periods, acceptance criteria, business availability, training obligations, and decommission milestones constrain the plan? Program leadership Determines delivery feasibility and partner estimates.
Proof Critical Which requirements must be proven through configured demonstrations, prototypes, reference calls, security evidence, or contractual commitments rather than written responses? Evaluation committee Focuses bidder effort on the highest-risk claims.

Appendix B

Infrastructure Requirements

52 infrastructure requirements across 11 sections — patching, hardware, storage, network, database, monitoring, ops, performance, business continuity, product roadmap and cloud. Source: Appendix B.

52 / 52

Infrastructure Architecture (IA)

5 requirements
IA001 M
The tenderer shall describe how its package is compliant to a patching / service pack policies of the underlying system components (OS, RDBMS…) and which procedure we should follow to keep those components up to date.
Our Response Fully Compliant with OOTB Features drafted by SE - Integration & Tools L2 (via WorkIQ) · 2026-09-18T14:40:25.457788
Verdict
Fully Compliant with OOTB Features
Vendor Comments
As a true SaaS offering, Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement and Power Platform operate under the Azure Shared Responsibility Model, which explicitly assigns Operating System, physical hosts, physical network, and datacenter patching entirely to Microsoft — BICS has zero OS or RDBMS patch obligations to discharge. Microsoft performs OS security updates, security hotfixes, and quality updates automatically during regional dark-hour maintenance windows via its Safe Deployment Process, rolling region-by-region through numbered Stations to minimise blast radius; administrators receive advance notification through the Microsoft 365 Message Center with at least five business days' notice for planned downtime. At the application layer, Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement receives weekly minor service updates and two mandatory major release waves per year (Wave 1 in April, Wave 2 in October), all backward-compatible and delivered touchlessly — BICS's procedure is limited to validating customisations in a sandbox environment before the wave reaches production, with the Power Platform admin centre providing version confirmation and configurable maintenance-window scheduling. For the underlying Dataverse SQL tier, Microsoft schedules and executes all database performance tuning, backup, and infrastructure updates automatically, as documented in the Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations Service Description responsibility matrix where 'Schedule regular infrastructure updates' is solely a Microsoft obligation.
Effort · Cost · Dependency
No BICS IT infrastructure patching effort is required for OS, RDBMS, or middleware layers; the only customer effort is regression-testing ISV and custom-connector solutions against the sandbox environment ahead of each bi-annual wave deployment, manageable within normal BAU change-management cycles.
Proximus-Specific Note
TeleSign and Route Mobile sit outside the Dynamics 365 / Power Platform SaaS boundary and are integrated via custom connectors or Azure API Management; their underlying API gateway and telecom platform patching remains the sole responsibility of TeleSign / Route Mobile respectively, and BICS should contractually require those vendors to provide equivalent patching SLAs. BICS-owned Azure integration middleware (e.g. Azure Logic Apps, Azure Service Bus) deployed for CPaaS bridging falls under PaaS shared responsibility, meaning Microsoft patches the runtime but BICS manages application-level updates to connector code and custom connector definitions.

IA002 M
The tenderer shall provide all scripts, setup programs, data needed to enable BICS to install/de-install the solution components.
Our Response Fully Compliant with Customization drafted by SE - Integration & Tools L2 (via WorkIQ) · 2026-09-18T14:41:44.973172
Verdict
Fully Compliant with Customization
Vendor Comments
The requirement to provide all scripts, setup programs, and data needed to install/de-install solution components is fully addressable in the Dynamics 365 and Power Platform SaaS model, though through cloud-native mechanisms rather than OS-level MSI packages. Customisation and configuration components are packaged as Dataverse managed solutions (solution.zip artifacts), deployable and removable via the Microsoft Power Platform CLI commands pac solution import, pac solution delete, and pac admin delete, or equivalently via Microsoft Power Platform Build Tools for Azure DevOps (PowerPlatformImportSolution, PowerPlatformDeleteSolution tasks) and GitHub Actions for Power Platform. Reference and configuration data required to seed an environment is transported using the Configuration Migration tool and the pac data import / pac data export commands, ensuring BICS receives a complete, repeatable deployment artefact set. Environment provisioning and decommissioning (the SaaS equivalent of install/uninstall) is scripted end-to-end using pac admin create and pac admin delete, and the full pipeline can be version-controlled in Git via Power Platform Pipelines extended with Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions.
Effort · Cost · Dependency
Microsoft must deliver: (1) a versioned Git repository containing all managed solution zip files, deployment settings JSON files, Configuration Migration data packages, and PAC CLI / Azure DevOps YAML pipeline scripts covering full install and uninstall sequences; (2) runbook documentation mapping each pipeline stage to the equivalent Appendix B install/uninstall step so BICS acceptance testers can validate end-to-end. Estimated effort is medium — the toolchain is fully OOTB but authoring and testing the complete deployment runbook for a Dynamics 365 Customer Service + Power Platform solution typically requires 3–5 sprint cycles in an ALM setup phase.
Proximus-Specific Note
TeleSign and Route Mobile bring no additional install/uninstall surface because their integration is exposed to Dynamics 365 exclusively through managed custom connectors and Power Automate flows, which are themselves packaged inside the same Dataverse managed solution artefact and removed atomically with pac solution delete. BICS should require that the solution package delivery checklist explicitly enumerates the custom connector definitions and flow bindings for TeleSign/Route Mobile so that decommissioning leaves no orphaned connection references in the tenant.

IA003 M
The tenderer shall provide the list of all system software (any third party or open source software) components included in the proposal . For open source software, He will mention the action taken to be compliant with component license ( as LGPL etc…) .
Our Response Fully Compliant with OOTB Features drafted by d365 · 2026-09-17T14:41:30.671586
Verdict
Fully Compliant with OOTB Features
Vendor Comments
As a pure SaaS offering, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Azure do not ship any installable system software to Proximus/BICS: there are no third-party binary packages, VMware drivers, Oracle JDBC JARs, or open-source runtime libraries that the customer must manage or license. Microsoft maintains a complete internal inventory of all open-source and third-party components embedded in the platform under its Security Development Lifecycle (SDL), including security analysis, continuous tracking, and an established incident-response process for vulnerable components. Per published Power Platform security documentation, the Component Governance process enforces integrity of all package sources and ensures only internally sourced packages are consumed, directly addressing OWASP A06 (Vulnerable and Outdated Components) and A08 (Software and Data Integrity Failures). Third-party software notices covering components used in Dynamics 365 and Azure services—including Apache 2.0, MIT, and related permissive OSS licences—are published by Microsoft on learn.microsoft.com/legal and are made available as part of the product's OSS compliance posture, with no copyleft (LGPL/GPL) obligations imposed on the customer.
Effort · Cost · Dependency
Zero customer effort is required for OSS licence compliance because Microsoft assumes full OSS stewardship responsibility as the SaaS operator. If Proximus commissions bespoke Power Platform solutions (plugins, PCF controls, Azure Functions), those custom components must carry their own OSS licence review, which is standard professional-services practice.
Proximus-Specific Note
BICS (TeleSign, Route Mobile) on-premise stacks manage their own OSS inventory (e.g., Java frameworks, Kubernetes operators, PostgreSQL) independently of the Microsoft SaaS layer, so no overlap or conflict arises. Delta analysis between BICS legacy on-prem OSS exposure and the Microsoft SaaS stack is not required by this RFP row.

IA004 M

Our Response Not Applicable drafted by SE - D365 (via WorkIQ) · 2026-09-18T11:05:46.145933
Verdict
Not Applicable
Vendor Comments
Dynamics 365 (Sales, Customer Service, Contact Center), Power Platform and Dataverse are delivered as multitenant SaaS/PaaS from Microsoft-operated Azure datacenters, so no IT infrastructure components are shipped to or installed in a BICS rack. Under the Microsoft shared responsibility model, physical hosts, physical network and physical datacenter are entirely Microsoft's responsibility for SaaS and PaaS, and customers consume a service-level agreement rather than hardware specifications. Microsoft therefore cannot supply 19-inch rack-mountable equipment, and none is required: datacenter facilities have redundant power, cooling and network connections with hardware redundancy at cluster and rack layers, operated by Microsoft onsite teams. Any residual BICS-side edge components (for example an on-premises data gateway for legacy system integration) run on BICS standard Windows Server hosts or Azure VMs and introduce no bespoke appliance.
Effort · Cost · Dependency
No effort or cost for hardware supply, racking, or datacenter delivery. Only effort is documenting the shared responsibility boundary and, if legacy connectivity is needed, sizing an on-premises data gateway on existing BICS standard hosts.
Proximus-Specific Note
Proximus Global (BICS, TeleSign, Route Mobile) is consolidating onto a cloud-first CRM, so this BICS-era on-premise HPE hardware clause does not carry across the merged entity; TeleSign and Route Mobile have no equivalent rack-delivery obligation for SaaS CRM. Recommend Appendix B is restated with SaaS-appropriate controls (SLA, regions, data residency, certifications) instead of rack form factor.

IA005 M
The tenderer shall guarantee that BICS would decide upon physical hostname of underlying system (no hardcoding allowed)
Our Response Not Applicable drafted by d365 · 2026-09-17T14:43:22.810434
Verdict
Not Applicable
Vendor Comments
Dynamics 365 and Power Platform are fully managed SaaS services hosted on Microsoft Azure; there are no physical servers, hostnames, or OS-level infrastructure exposed to or configurable by the customer. Vendor Comments
Dynamics 365 and Power Platform SaaS production environments are deployed across at least two, and typically three, Azure Availability Zones per geography, each with physically independent power, cooling, and networking, delivering in-region failover with near-zero RPO and an RTO of under five minutes for Dynamics 365 CE (under 30 minutes for Finance & Operations) with no manual intervention required. For cross-datacentre distance greater than the intra-region zone separation, Power Platform Self-Service Disaster Recovery (SSDR) — generally available since April 30, 2025 for Dataverse workloads, and extended to Finance & Operations on June 22, 2026 — asynchronously replicates production environments to an Azure paired region typically separated by at least 300 miles, with typical replication lag under 15 minutes and often under five minutes, and admin-initiated failover and failback executed directly from the Power Platform Admin Center. Dynamics 365 databases leverage Azure SQL Database active geo-replication and document attachments use geo-redundant Azure Blob Storage copies in the paired region, as documented in the Dynamics 365 service description, with DR procedures attested annually through SOC 2 Type II audits available on the Microsoft Service Trust Portal. SSDR requires the environment to be designated as a Managed Environment, which is automatically satisfied by most Dynamics 365 commercial licence tiers, and the Power Platform Admin Center exposes real-time replication-lag telemetry so BICS can monitor RPO continuously and run compliance drills against a secondary-region copy without production downtime.
Effort · Cost · Dependency
Zero infrastructure effort is required from BICS for intra-region availability-zone failover, which is fully managed by Microsoft OOTB. Enabling cross-region SSDR requires a one-time admin action in the Power Platform Admin Center to activate the secondary-region replica, and firewall allow-lists must be extended to include the paired Azure region's outbound IP ranges if network-level access controls are in place.
Proximus-Specific Note
Proximus/BICS operates primarily out of Belgium; the corresponding Azure geography is West Europe (Netherlands) with North Europe (Ireland) as its paired DR region, both within EU boundaries, satisfying Belgian and EU data-residency obligations that apply equally to TeleSign and Route Mobile workloads absorbed post-merger. TeleSign and Route Mobile workloads migrated onto the Dynamics 365 CRM platform inherit the same OOTB BCDR architecture without delta; no incremental DR configuration is required beyond ensuring all entity data is consolidated into the single production Dataverse environment covered by SSDR.

Vendor Comments
Dynamics 365 and Power Platform run on Microsoft Dataverse, a multitenant SaaS service where each tenant is a separate Microsoft Entra ID directory and each environment is an isolated Dataverse instance with its own database, acting as a hard security boundary between applications and data. Microsoft 365/Azure isolation controls combine Entra ID authentication and authorization, container/compute and network isolation, and storage segregation so that one tenant's data is never accessible from another tenant's compute or identity context, with continuous automated monitoring and red-team testing of tenant boundaries. Within a tenant, Dataverse enforces role-based security, business units as security boundaries, record (row) ownership and sharing, hierarchy security and column-level (field-level) security, so CRM data for different Proximus Global brands and applications is separated logically and by configuration. All data at rest is encrypted by default using Azure SQL Transparent Data Encryption and Azure Storage encryption with Microsoft-managed keys, and customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault can be enabled per environment for stronger cryptographic separation; DLP policies restrict connector-level data flows between environments.
Effort · Cost · Dependency
No development effort: isolation between Microsoft customers is platform-native and non-configurable, and intra-tenant separation is delivered through standard environment, business unit, security role, field-level security and DLP configuration during the design phase. Optional customer-managed key enablement requires an Azure Key Vault setup and an environment enterprise policy (configuration, not custom code).
Proximus-Specific Note
For the BICS / TeleSign / Route Mobile consolidation, we recommend one Proximus Global tenant with separate production environments (or at minimum separate business units plus modernized business unit record ownership) per entity, so wholesale voice/messaging, fraud/identity and CPaaS customer data stay separated while enabling controlled cross-sell visibility. Entity-specific confidentiality (e.g. TeleSign identity data and carrier commercial terms) can be further protected with column-level security and per-environment customer-managed keys.

ZoomInfo is documented by Microsoft as a first-party-supported data enrichment integration for Dynamics 365 Sales: it installs as a native Marketplace solution package that syncs firmographic data (company size, revenue, industry, zoominfoid) directly into Dataverse Account, Contact, and Lead tables, and those Dataverse fields are then consumed by the Sales Qualification Agent and Copilot for Sales for lead scoring and enrichment. Microsoft has no own B2B intent-signal and go-to-market prospecting database of comparable depth, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator (the nearest Microsoft-native substitute) covers professional identity and network graph but does not replicate ZoomInfo's technographic, intent, or bulk prospecting dataset.
Proposed capability
Dynamics 365 Sales (Sales Hub / Sales Qualification Agent) via native ZoomInfo Marketplace app writing into Dataverse; Copilot for Sales extensibility for in-context enrichment surfaced in Outlook and Teams; optionally Customer Insights – Data for unified profile enrichment from ZoomInfo-populated Dataverse fields.
Connector / dev posture
Standard connector: No · 3rd-party still required: True · Custom dev: True
Gaps / limitations
There is no Microsoft-published certified Power Platform connector for ZoomInfo in the connector gallery; the integration is delivered as a Marketplace solution package (install via Power Apps portal, not the standard connector framework), meaning Proximus Global must contact ZoomInfo to receive the package and field-mapping is manual configuration, not a turn-key connector. For Copilot for Sales in-context enrichment (opportunity insights, record details), a custom Power Platform connector exposing ZoomInfo APIs with OAuth 2.0 + Microsoft Entra ID must be built by ZoomInfo or Proximus, then registered as a Copilot Studio action — this is documented as a preview extensibility pattern and each connector API must respond within 5 seconds. LinkedIn Sales Navigator (Microsoft Relationship Sales SKU) partially overlaps on contact/company intelligence and is deeply embedded in D365 Sales natively, but cannot replace ZoomInfo's technographic, intent-signal, or bulk-prospecting dataset used by BICS and TeleSign.
Licence / cost drivers
Dynamics 365 Sales Enterprise (required for ZoomInfo Marketplace app and Sales Qualification Agent); Copilot for Sales (for in-context enrichment in Outlook/Teams via connector action); ZoomInfo subscription and per-seat export licence (third-party cost, retained); Copilot Studio (for connector action registration and management); Microsoft Relationship Sales add-on if LinkedIn Sales Navigator is deployed alongside ZoomInfo.
Assumptions
ZoomInfo retains its own subscription licence and data export quotas; the Proximus Global Dynamics 365 environment runs on Unified Interface (Sales Hub) with Dataverse as the CRM data store, which is required for the native ZoomInfo Marketplace solution package.
Proximus-Specific Note
For BICS (B2B wholesale telecom) and TeleSign (CPaaS), ZoomInfo's technographic and intent-signal data is operationally critical for identifying enterprise buyers with relevant tech stacks and buying signals — Microsoft's LinkedIn Sales Navigator is complementary (relationship intelligence, org charts) but cannot replace ZoomInfo's prospecting database depth for these specific go-to-market motions. Proximus Global should negotiate with ZoomInfo to prioritise delivery of a certified Power Platform connector or at minimum a stable OpenAPI definition, as the current install-via-package model creates a governance and ALM risk in an enterprise CRM programme of this scale.

Our Response Yes drafted by SE - Security & Compliance L2 (via WorkIQ) · 2026-09-18T16:02:21.656726
Answer
Yes

Specifically certified and independently attested standards include: ISO/IEC 27017:2015 (cloud-specific security controls — certificate at servicetrust.microsoft.com/DocumentPage/e7beae4b-1648-4626-a5a5-94d452c37fa8, latest report date June 9, 2026); ISO/IEC 27018:2019 (protection of PII in the cloud — certificate at servicetrust.microsoft.com/DocumentPage/0ab61d82-abd5-42fe-a950-eab7390585dc, latest report date June 9, 2026); ISO/IEC 27701:2019 (privacy information management, extension to ISO 27001/27018, covering all controls — certificate at servicetrust.microsoft.com/DocumentPage/68e67c6e-a1b7-4c96-a04d-ae0a298bf2c2, latest report date June 9, 2026); ISO 22301:2019 (business continuity management — certificate at servicetrust.microsoft.com/DocumentPage/89e00637-1937-4dd0-8081-9ed95b1ae242, latest report date October 31, 2025); ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 (IT service management, covering Azure, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform); SOC 1 Type 2 (latest report January 30, 2026, at servicetrust.microsoft.com/DocumentPage/3d548eee-9227-40c0-8464-3a6ec3980657); SOC 2 Type 2 (latest report January 30, 2026, at servicetrust.microsoft.com/DocumentPage/4e65cc45-86be-46d6-b0c5-0db631708295); SOC 3 (publicly available); PCI DSS Level 1 (including PCI DSS, PCI PIN, and PCI 3DS packages available at servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/PCI); HIPAA BAA; FedRAMP High (latest report June 26, 2026, at servicetrust.microsoft.com/DocumentPage/34734523-5afd-4ca2-b536-8a642c9da231); Germany BSI C5 (Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue); Australia IRAP (Information Security Registered Assessors Program); and CSA STAR Certification and Attestation. For Proximus as a Belgian operator, the EU Data Boundary commitment is directly relevant: Azure, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform data can be stored and processed exclusively within EU/EFTA datacenters (France, Germany, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland, Poland, Italy, Ireland, Netherlands) by provisioning in the 'European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA)' macro region geography. Data protection is further governed by the Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum (DPA, at aka.ms/dpa) and Microsoft Product Terms, binding contractual instruments. Microsoft Purview solutions (including Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, Microsoft Purview Information Protection with sensitivity labels, Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention, Microsoft Purview Audit, and Microsoft Purview Customer Lockbox) provide in-platform controls mapped to these certifications. Microsoft Priva (Privacy Risk Management and Subject Rights Requests) and Microsoft Defender for Cloud (with regulatory compliance dashboard supporting ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and SOC 2 benchmarks) complete the governance and evidence layer. All certificates and audit reports can be downloaded from the Microsoft Service Trust Portal (servicetrust.microsoft.com) under the ISO, SOC, and PCI sections.

Our glossary — the concepts we use to answer

Every Microsoft, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Azure, Copilot, Purview and Entra term used in our Appendix A answers, defined in plain business language with a note on where it appears and what it costs. 87 terms curated · 70 actually used in the current draft.

Dataverse
Platform foundation
Microsoft's low-code enterprise data platform — the shared, secure, governed database that sits underneath Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.
Show detail
Dataverse stores the Account, Contact, Opportunity, Case, Product and thousands of other tables that Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service ship with, plus any custom tables Proximus Global adds. It provides role-based security, field-level security, auditing, hierarchies, business rules, workflows, plug-ins, virtual tables, elastic tables, change tracking, Web API/OData endpoints and out-of-the-box connectors. Every answer in this RFP that says 'stored in Dataverse' means the data lives in one governed store shared across BICS, TeleSign and Route Mobile — no duplicated CRM database per brand.
Licensing: Included with Dynamics 365 Enterprise licences; standalone via Power Apps per-app or per-user plans.
Used in 150 answers e.g. CRM-001, CRM-002, CRM-003, CRM-005, CRM-006

PXG Reference

Proximus Global vocabulary

21 business terms Proximus Global uses in the requirements matrix. This is their vocabulary. For the Microsoft/D365 terms we use in our answers, see the Our Glossary tab.

Term / Business ConceptDefinitionClarification / ScopeRelated Category
Customer / Commercial EntityExternal organisation managed in the CRM because it has, or may have, a commercial or contractual relationship with Proximus Global entities.This concept is used to remain vendor-neutral. Depending on the CRM platform, the equivalent object may be called Account, Customer, Company, Organisation, Business Partner or similar. Internal suppliers/vendors are excluded unless explicitly stated otherwise.Customer & Commercial Entity Management; Account & Contact Management
AccountCurrent terminology referring to a customer, prospect, reseller, partner or other external commercial entity managed in CRM.In the RFP matrix, this term should preferably be interpreted as Customer / Commercial Entity to avoid confusion with financial/accounting accounts.Customer & Commercial Entity Management
ContactIndividual person associated with a customer, prospect, partner or other commercial entity.Contacts may have different roles in sales, contract, support, portal access or operational processes.Contact Management
Product and Billing ArrangementInternal CRM business record capturing the operational, commercial, financial and product configuration required to conduct business with a customer.A Product and Billing Arrangement is not a legal contract or contractual document. It is used as an operational business entity supporting downstream processes such as provisioning, pricing, invoicing, inventory management, fulfilment and customer care. It may contain customer relationship information, product/service information, billing configuration, accounting information, validity periods and operational attributes required by downstream systems.Product and Billing Arrangement
ContractContractual document or legal agreement managed through contract lifecycle management processes.Legal Contracts may include negotiation, review, approval, signature, renewal, expiration and contractual clauses.Contract Management
OpportunityCommercial sales opportunity representing a potential business deal, revenue opportunity or commercial initiative with a customer or prospect.The platform should support the opportunity lifecycle independently from the vendor-specific object name or implementation model.Opportunity Management
LeadPotential customer, contact or business opportunity that requires qualification before conversion into downstream CRM records.The lead process may include capture, enrichment, routing, qualification, scoring and conversion.Lead Management
Product / ServiceCommercial offering that can be sold, bought, configured, quoted, contracted, provisioned, billed or supported.Products and services may include telecom-specific offerings such as voice, messaging, roaming or other PXG services.Product Catalogue & CPQ
Product InformationProduct or service information captured within a Product and Billing Arrangement to enable the operational and financial management of the customer relationship.This information may be used by pricing, provisioning, invoicing, inventory and customer care processes.Product and Billing Arrangement; Product Catalogue & CPQ
Product and Billing Arrangement Billing InformationBilling and invoicing configuration captured within a Product and Billing Arrangement.Examples may include billing address, invoice classification, accounting company, currency, VAT status, payment terms and billing cycle. These examples provide business context and do not prescribe a specific CRM data model.Product and Billing Arrangement
Product and Billing Arrangement Validity PeriodStart date, end date or other lifecycle dates defining when the Product and Billing Arrangement and related operational processes are effective.Validity periods may be used by downstream processes such as provisioning, pricing, invoicing and customer care.Product and Billing Arrangement
Sender IDTelecom-related business process for managing sender identities used in messaging services.The CRM capability should support request intake, validation, approval, fulfilment tracking and customer communication, either natively or through integrations.Customer Support
Service Centre PortalCustomer support or service portal capability used for case submission, tracking and communication.The term is used generically and does not prescribe a specific vendor portal technology.Customer Self-Service & Portal; Customer Support
Approval ProcessStructured validation or decision workflow used to approve business records, requests or changes.Approval processes may apply to opportunities, contracts, commercial agreements, support requests, product-related processes or other CRM workflows.Approval Process
CampaignMarketing or sales initiative used to target, engage or track a group of leads, contacts, customers or prospects.Campaign-related capabilities may include campaign members, attribution, influence analysis and reporting.Campaign Management; Marketing & Sales Enablement
Data EnrichmentCapability to improve CRM data by adding, validating or enhancing information from internal or external sources.Examples may include enrichment of leads, contacts or customer/commercial entity data through third-party data providers or internal data sources.Data Enrichment; Data Quality & Deduplication
Data Quality & DeduplicationCapabilities used to prevent, detect, monitor, remediate and merge duplicate or poor-quality CRM records.This includes matching rules, duplicate detection, merge/survivorship, data quality monitoring and stewardship workflows.Data Quality & Deduplication
Outlook & Teams IntegrationIntegration between the CRM platform and Microsoft Outlook, Teams or equivalent collaboration tools.Expected capabilities may include email tracking, calendar synchronisation, task and event management, collaboration and activity capture subject to security and privacy controls.Outlook & Teams Integration
OOTB FeaturesStandard product capabilities available through configuration, parameterisation or standard platform setup.No custom development, custom code or non-standard extension is required.Compliance Definitions
CustomizationNon-standard implementation work required to meet a requirement beyond standard platform configuration.This may include custom development, extensions, integrations, custom objects, custom workflows or third-party components.Compliance Definitions

Compliance response codes (Appendix A)

CodeDefinition
Fully Compliant with OOTB FeaturesRequirement fully supported through standard product capabilities and configuration only. No custom development required.
Fully Compliant with CustomizationRequirement fully supported but requires custom development, extensions or integrations beyond standard configuration.
Future CompliantRequirement not currently supported but planned on the product roadmap. Specify expected availability date and licensing implications.
Partially CompliantRequirement only partially supported. Explain limitations, gaps and any proposed workaround.
Not CompliantRequirement cannot be supported by the proposed solution, either through standard capabilities or customisation. Alternative approaches may be provided where applicable.
Rule: Vendor selects only one compliance option per requirement. Use X in the relevant column and provide comments where requested. For any response other than Fully Compliant OOTB, provide assumptions, limitations, dependencies, effort estimates and licensing / implementation costs.
